question.problem:
The values of functions $h(x)$ and $z(x)$ and their derivatives at $t=3$ are given in the table below.

| $t$ | $h(t)$ | $z(t)$ | ${h}^{′}(t)$ | ${z}^{′}(t)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $3$ | $-2$ | $6$ | $5$ | $-1$ |

If $f(t)=\frac{2+h(t)}{z(t)},$ compute  ${f}^{′}(3).$ Do not round the answer.

${f}^{′}(3)=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
The quotient rule states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{u}{v})=\frac{{u}^{′}v-u{v}^{′}}{{v}^{2}}.
$$

Let $u=2+h(t)$ and $v=z(t).$ Differentiating each, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t}={h}^{′}(t)\,\text{and}\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}={z}^{′}(t).
$$

Substituting into the quotient rule gives

$$
{f}^{′}(t)=\frac{{h}^{′}(t)z(t)-(2+h(t)){z}^{′}(t)}{{z}^{2}(t)}.
$$

At $t=3,$ this gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(3) & =\frac{{h}^{′}(3)z(3)-(2+h(3)){z}^{′}(3)}{{z}^{2}(3)} \\  & =\frac{5\cdot 6-(2+(-2))(-1)}{{6}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{30-(0)(-1)}{36} \\  & =\frac{30}{36} \\  & =\frac{5}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$
